title: How much chikki did {{NAME_1}} and the younger brother eat together?
description: {{NAME_1}} eats one half of a chikki and the younger brother eats one fourth. Cutting the whole into fourths lets us count both shares in the same unit. Keeko doubts the answer by adding the tops and adding the bottoms.
teaching_notes: One idea: to add two shares, cut them into the same fractional unit and count the pieces. Watch for the slip of adding the tops and adding the bottoms.

source: {{NAME_1}}'s father made some chikki. {{NAME_1}} ate 1/2 of it and her
video_script.why: A learner adds one half and one fourth by seeing the half as two fourths, so both shares count the same fractional unit.
video_script.substitution: the book's own chikki, cut into halves and then into fourths
video_script.anchor: a chikki cut into two halves, with one half cut again into two fourths
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds the tops and adds the bottoms and gets two sixths. Two sixths is the same as one third, which is less than the half {{NAME_1}} ate alone, so the idea is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: together they ate three fourths of the chikki
video_script.fraction_reading: one half, one fourth, two fourths, three fourths, two sixths, one third

names.{{NAME_1}}: eats one half of the chikki her father made

never_show: two sixths written as the sum before Keeko's doubt
maths_rules: the whole chikki is cut into 4 equal pieces; each piece is 1/4
the younger brother eats 1 piece of 1/4
slip: Keeko adds the tops and the bottoms and gets 2/6; 2/6 = 1/3, which is less than 1/2, the share eaten alone
video_script.design: One chikki strip stays on the board. It is cut into halves, then the second half into fourths, and the pieces are counted in fourths.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a chikki strip with one half shaded in teal and one fourth shaded in amber; the words eat together? appear

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears and the chikki strip appears
marks.eat: one half of the strip is shaded in teal and one fourth of it in amber

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is from your book, where {{NAME_1}}'s father has made some chikki.
<bookmark mark='eat'/>{{NAME_1}} eats one half of it, and {{NAME_1}}'s younger brother eats one fourth.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How much of the chikki do they eat together?

beats.on_screen: the chikki strip holds still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a chikki strip is cut into two halves, then one half is cut into two equal pieces; a note says same amount, smaller pieces

marks.cut: a strip is cut into two halves, and then one half is cut into two equal pieces
marks.unit: the note same amount, smaller pieces appears beside the cut half
marks.goal: pieces of one size are boxed together

narration: <bookmark mark='cut'/>Cut a chikki into two halves, and then cut one half into two equal pieces.
<bookmark mark='unit'/>Cutting into smaller equal pieces keeps the amount the same, but it changes the fractional unit.
<bookmark mark='goal'/>To add two shares, we count them in pieces of one size.

beats.on_screen: Given: 1/2 of the chikki eaten by {{NAME_1}}, 1/4 of it eaten by the younger brother
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, {{NAME_1}} eats one half of the chikki and the younger brother eats one fourth.

beats.on_screen: To find: how much chikki they ate together
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how much of the chikki they eat together.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: cut the whole chikki into 4 equal pieces; each piece is 1/4

marks.cut: the whole strip is cut into four equal pieces

narration: <bookmark mark='cut'/>Step one, cut the whole chikki into four equal pieces.
<bookmark mark='unit'/>Each piece is one fourth of the whole chikki.

marks.half: the half is shaded and covers two of the four pieces

narration: <bookmark mark='half'/>Step two, the half that {{NAME_1}} eats covers two of these pieces.
<bookmark mark='same'/>One half is the same as one fourth plus one fourth.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: add the brother's 1 piece: 1/2 + 1/4 = 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 3 x 1/4

marks.add: one more piece of 1/4 is shaded in amber

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, the younger brother eats one more piece of one fourth.
<bookmark mark='count'/>One half plus one fourth is one fourth plus one fourth plus one fourth. That is three times one fourth.

marks.ans: 3/4 of the chikki is written and glows

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Three times one fourth is three fourths, so together they ate three fourths of the chikki.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the chikki strip
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says add the tops and add the bottoms: 2/6; a strip of 6 equal pieces with 2 shaded sits under the half and is shorter; the bubble is struck out

marks.doubt: the bubble with the wrong idea appears
marks.short: a strip of six equal pieces with two shaded sits under the half and is shorter

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks they ate two sixths, because one plus one is two and two plus four is six.
<bookmark mark='short'/>Two sixths is the same as one third of the chikki. That is less than the half that {{NAME_1}} ate alone.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Adding more cannot give less, so we count both shares in the same fractional unit.
